newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia truckers agree to end strike, gov't says.
newsitem.headline: Colombia truckers agree to end strike, gov't says.

text.p: Colombia's main truck drivers' union has agreed to end a six-day-old work stoppage, the Transportation Ministry said in a statement Friday.

"At the end of 22 hours of talks between the government and members of the Colombian Truck Drivers' Association, an accord was reached to end the strike by truckers that had been going on since last Sunday," the statement said.

Union officials could not be reached for immediate comment. But they said earlier that their strike, which reportedly paralyzed virtually all highway freight, would only be lifted once President Ernesto Samper personally endorsed all agreements worked out in marathon talks at the Transportation Ministry's offices in downtown Bogota.

A decree, vouching for the agreements and specifying that the government had agreed to a key demand for the setting of minimum cargo rates for highway freight, was issued by the presidential palace shortly after the Transportation Ministry's announcement.
